title.zh: 卷一百五十四 列傳第一百〇四: 孔巢父 許孟容 呂元膺 劉棲楚 張宿 熊望 柏耆
title.en: Volume 154 Biographies 104: Kong Chaofu, Xu Mengrong, Lu Yuanying, Liu Qichu, Zhang Su, Xiong Wang, Bai Qi
title.raw: 卷一百五十四 列傳第一百〇四: 孔巢父 許孟容 呂元膺 劉棲楚 張宿 熊望 柏耆 Volume 154 Biographies 104: Kong Chaofu, Xu Mengrong, Lu Yuanying, Liu Qichu, Zhang Su, Xiong Wang, Bai Qi

sentences.zh: 孔巢父，冀州人，字弱翁。

translations.literal: Kong Chaofu was a man of Jizhou; his courtesy name was Ruo'eng.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu came from Jizhou; his courtesy name was Ruo'eng.

sentences.zh: 父如珪，海州司戶參軍，以巢父贈工部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Ru Gui was Registrar of the Revenue Bureau in Haizhou; because of Chaofu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru Gui had been Registrar of Haizhou; Chaofu's career earned him a posthumous appointment as Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 巢父早勤文史，少時與韓準、裴政、李白、張叔明、陶沔隱於徂來山，時號「竹溪六逸」。

translations.literal: Chaofu from early on diligently cultivated literature and historiography; in youth he secluded himself on Mount Culaith with Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Li Bai, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Yan, and at the time they were styled the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek."
translations.idiomatic: From an early age Chaofu devoted himself to letters and learning. As a young man he lived in seclusion on Mount Culaith with Han Zhun, Pei Zheng, Li Bai, Zhang Shuming, and Tao Yan—they were known at the time as the "Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek."

sentences.zh: 永王璘起兵江淮，聞其賢，以從事辟之。

translations.literal: When Prince Yong Li Lin raised an army in the Jianghuai region, hearing of his worth he summoned him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yong Li Lin took up arms in the Jianghuai region, he heard of Chaofu's reputation and recruited him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 巢父知其必敗，側身潛遁，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chaofu knew he would necessarily fail, turned aside and fled in secret, and thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu saw that the enterprise was doomed, slipped away unnoticed, and thereby made his name known.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，李季卿為江淮宣撫使，薦巢父，授左衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the Guangde reign period Li Jiqing served as Pacification Commissioner of Jianghuai, recommended Chaofu, and he was appointed Army Registrar of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangde, when Li Jiqing was Pacification Commissioner for the Jianghuai region, he recommended Chaofu, who was then made Army Registrar of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，澤潞節度使李抱玉奏為賓幕，累授監察御史，轉殿中、檢校庫部員外郎，出授歸州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali reign period the Military Governor of Ze-Lu Li Baoyu memorialized him to the staff, and he was successively appointed Investigating Censor, transferred to Palace Censor, Acting Assistant Director in the Ministry of Treasury, and sent out as Prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dali, Li Baoyu, military governor of Ze and Lu, brought him onto his staff. He rose through the posts of Investigating Censor and Palace Censor to Acting Assistant Director in the Ministry of Treasury, then was sent out as prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 建中初，涇原節度留後孟皞表巢父試秘書少監，兼御史中丞、行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign period the Acting Military Governor of Jingyuan Meng Hao memorialized Chaofu to probationary Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, Meng Hao, acting governor of Jingyuan, recommended Chaofu for probationary Vice Director of the Secretariat, with concurrent posts as Vice Censor-in-Chief and campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 尋拜汾州刺史，入為諫議大夫，出為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Fenzhou, entered the capital as Remonstrating Adviser, and went out as Prefect of Tanzhou and Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Fenzhou, recalled to the capital as Remonstrating Adviser, then sent out again as prefect of Tanzhou and observation commissioner for Hunan.

sentences.zh: 未行，會普王為荊襄副元帥，以巢父為元帥府行軍司馬，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before he had set out, it happened that Prince Pu was made Deputy Supreme Commander of Jing-Xiang, and Chaofu was made Campaigning Grand Marshal of the supreme commander's headquarters, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the Hunan post, Prince Pu was named deputy supreme commander for Jing and Xiang; Chaofu was appointed campaigning marshal on his staff with the concurrent title of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋屬涇師之難，從德宗幸奉天，遷給事中、河中陜華等州招討使。

translations.literal: Soon it fell in the time of the Jing Army disaster; he followed Dezong in his flight to Fengtian, was promoted to Attendant at the Secretariat, and made Pacification Commissioner of the Hezhong, Shanzhou, and Huazhou circuit et al.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward came the mutiny of the Jing army; he accompanied Dezong to Fengtian and was promoted to Attendant at the Secretariat and made pacification commissioner for Hezhong, Shaanxi, Huazhou, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 累獻破賊之謀，德宗甚賞之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented plans for defeating the rebels, and Dezong greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted plan after plan for crushing the rebels, and Dezong was highly impressed.

sentences.zh: 尋兼御史大夫，充魏博宣慰使。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Censor-in-Chief and commissioned as Reassurance Commissioner to Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the concurrent post of Censor-in-Chief and sent as reassurance commissioner to Weibo.

sentences.zh: 巢父博辯多智，對田悅之眾，陳逆順利害君臣之道，士眾欣悚喜抃，曰：「不圖今日復睹王化！」

translations.literal: Chaofu was broadly eloquent and greatly resourceful; facing Tian Yue's troops he expounded the principles of right and wrong, advantage and harm, and the way of ruler and minister; the officers and soldiers were delighted and awestruck, clapping their hands for joy, saying: "We never expected that today we would again behold royal civilization!
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu was eloquent and shrewd. Before Tian Yue's assembled forces he explained what loyalty and rebellion meant, the gains and losses at stake, and the obligations of subject to sovereign. The troops were thrilled and moved, exclaiming with joy, "We never thought we would live to see the court's authority restored!

sentences.zh: 及就宴，悅酒酣，自矜其騎射之藝、拳勇之略，因曰：「若蒙見用，無堅不摧。」

translations.literal: When they came to the banquet, Yue, being deep in wine, vaunted his skill in horsemanship and archery and his prowess in boxing and valor, and accordingly said: "If I am employed, nothing stout will I fail to smash."
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet Yue, well into his cups, boasted of his horsemanship and archery and of his strength and daring, and added, "If the throne would only use me, there is no fortress I could not break."

sentences.zh: 巢父謂之曰：「若如公言而不早歸國者，但為一好賊耳。」

translations.literal: Chaofu said to him: "If it is as you say and yet you do not early return to allegiance to the state, you are merely a fine bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu replied, "If what you say is true and you still will not submit to the court, you are nothing but an accomplished rebel."

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「為賊既曰好賊，為臣當作功臣。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "If as a bandit one is called a fine bandit, as a minister one ought to be made a meritorious minister."
translations.idiomatic: Yue answered, "If a rebel can be a 'fine rebel,' then a loyal minister ought to become a celebrated servant of the state."

sentences.zh: 巢父曰：「國方有虞，待子而息。」

translations.literal: Chaofu said: "The state is just now in peril; it awaits you to quiet it."
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu said, "The realm is in turmoil; it is waiting for you to bring it peace."

sentences.zh: 悅起謝焉。

translations.literal: Yue rose and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue rose and thanked him for the words.

sentences.zh: 悅背叛日久，其下厭亂，且喜巢父之至。

translations.literal: Yue had rebelled for a long time; his subordinates were weary of disorder and moreover rejoiced at Chaofu's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had been in rebellion for years; his men were sick of the turmoil and welcomed Chaofu's arrival.

sentences.zh: 數日，田承嗣之子緒以失職怨望，因人心之搖動，遂構謀殺悅，而與大將邢曹俊等稟命於巢父。

translations.literal: Several days later, Tian Chengsi's son Xu, resentful over loss of office, taking advantage of the swaying of men's hearts, thereupon plotted to kill Yue, and with the great general Xing Cao Jun and others reported to Chaofu for orders.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Tian Chengsi's son Xu, angry over being stripped of his post, exploited the restlessness among the ranks and plotted to kill Yue, then sought Chaofu's approval together with the senior general Xing Cao Jun and others.

sentences.zh: 巢父因其眾意，令田緒權知軍務，以紓其難。

translations.literal: Chaofu, following the will of the masses, ordered Tian Xu to provisionally handle military affairs, thereby easing the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the mood of the army, Chaofu had Tian Xu take temporary charge of military affairs, which defused the crisis.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，李懷光擁兵河中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan Li Huai'guang held troops in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan (784), Li Huai'guang held Hezhong with his army.

sentences.zh: 七月，復以巢父兼御史大夫，充宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he again made Chaofu concurrent Censor-in-Chief and commissioned him as Reassurance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chaofu was again named Censor-in-Chief and sent out as reassurance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既傳詔旨，懷光以巢父嘗使魏博，田悅死於帳下，恐禍及。

translations.literal: Once the imperial edict had been transmitted, Huai'guang, because Chaofu had once been envoy to Weibo and Tian Yue had died under his tent, feared disaster would reach him.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was read aloud, Huai'guang remembered that Chaofu had once been envoy to Weibo and that Tian Yue had died in his camp; he feared the same fate awaited him.

sentences.zh: 又朔方蕃渾之眾數千，皆在行列，頗驕悖不肅。

translations.literal: Moreover several thousand troops of the Shuofang Tongluo tribes were all in the ranks, quite arrogant and insubordinate and not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Shuofang tribal cavalry were also in the ranks, arrogant and ill-disciplined.

sentences.zh: 聞罷懷光兵權，時懷光素服待命，巢父不止之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Huai'guang's military authority was to be removed, at the time Huai'guang was in plain dress awaiting orders; Chaofu did not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that Huai'guang was to be stripped of his command, the troops grew unruly even though Huai'guang sat in mourning garb awaiting the edict; Chaofu did nothing to stop them.

sentences.zh: 眾鹹忿恚，咄嗟曰：「太尉盡無官矣！」

translations.literal: The crowd all were indignant, exclaiming in anger: "The Grand Marshal has completely lost his offices!
translations.idiomatic: The men erupted in fury, shouting, "The Grand Marshal has lost every post!

sentences.zh: 方宣詔，喧噪，懷光亦不禁止，巢父、守盈並遇害。

translations.literal: Just as the edict was being proclaimed, there was clamor and uproar; Huai'guang also did not restrain them; Chaofu and Shou Ying were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: As the edict was being proclaimed the camp erupted in uproar. Huai'guang made no move to restrain his men, and both Chaofu and Shou Ying were killed.

sentences.zh: 上聞之震悼，贈尚書左僕射，仍詔收河中日備禮葬祭。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing of it, was shocked and grieved, enfeoffed him posthumously as Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and moreover ordered that within one day in Hezhong he be buried and sacrificed to with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong heard the news he was stunned with grief. Chaofu was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and orders went out that his body be recovered in Hezhong and buried with full honors within a single day.

sentences.zh: 賜其家布帛米粟甚厚，仍授子正員官。

translations.literal: His family was given cloth, silk, rice, and grain in great abundance, and moreover his son was granted a full regular office.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave his family a lavish grant of cloth, grain, and provisions and appointed his son to a regular court post.

sentences.zh: 從子戡、戣、戢。

translations.literal: His nephews were Kan, Wei, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews were Kong Kan, Kong Wei, and Kong Ji.

sentences.zh: 戡，巢父兄岑父之子。

translations.literal: Kan was the son of Chaofu's elder brother Cenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kan was the son of Chaofu's elder brother Cenfu.

sentences.zh: 方嚴有家法，重然諾，尚忠義。

translations.literal: Upright and stern in family discipline, he valued promises kept and esteemed loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and principled, he observed strict household discipline, kept his word, and prized loyalty.

sentences.zh: 盧從史鎮澤潞，辟為書記。

translations.literal: When Lu Congshi governed Ze-Lu, he summoned him as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Congshi became military governor of Ze and Lu, he recruited Kan as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 從史浸驕，與王承宗、田緒陰相連結，欲效河朔事以固其位。

translations.literal: Congshi gradually grew arrogant, secretly linked himself with Wang Chengzong and Tian Xu, and wished to imitate the Hebei affairs to solidify his position.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi grew increasingly overbearing, secretly aligned himself with Wang Chengzong and Tian Xu, and sought to copy the semi-independent warlord model of the Hebei provinces to cement his own position.

sentences.zh: 戡每秉筆至不軌之言，極諫以為不可，從史怒戡，歲餘，謝病歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Whenever Kan took the brush to unorthodox statements, he remonstrated to the utmost that it could not be done; Congshi was angry at Kan; after more than a year he pleaded illness and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kan was asked to draft disloyal proposals, he argued passionately that they must not be done. Congshi was furious; after a year and more Kan pleaded illness and retired to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫鎮揚州，召為賓佐。

translations.literal: Li Jifu governed Yangzhou and summoned him as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu governed Yangzhou he brought Kan onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 從史知之，上疏論列，請行貶逐。

translations.literal: Congshi learned of it and memorialized enumerating his faults, requesting that he be demoted and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi learned of this and memorialized the court, demanding Kan's demotion and banishment.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不得已，授衛尉丞，分司洛陽。

translations.literal: Xianzong had no alternative and appointed him Assistant Director in the Court of the Imperial Stud, with duty station at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong reluctantly appointed him Assistant Director in the Court of the Imperial Stud, with nominal duty at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元中籓帥誣奏從事者，皆不驗理，便行降黜。

translations.literal: Previously, in the Zhenyuan reign period when regional commanders falsely memorialized against staff members, without verifying the case they would at once demote them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenyuan, when a regional commander slandered a staff member the court almost never investigated; the man was simply demoted.

sentences.zh: 及戡詔下，給事中呂元膺執之，上令中使慰喻元膺，制書方下。

translations.literal: When Kan's edict came down, Attendant at the Secretariat Lu Yuanying held it fast; the emperor ordered a palace envoy to comfort and instruct Yuanying, and only then did the imperial rescript issue.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict against Kan was drafted, Attendant Lu Yuanying blocked it. The emperor sent an envoy to persuade him, and only then was the appointment issued.

sentences.zh: 戡不調而卒，贈駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: Kan died before taking up the post, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Imperial Accouterments.
translations.idiomatic: Kan died before he could take up the post and was posthumously made Assistant Director in the Bureau of Imperial Accouterments.

sentences.zh: 戣，字君嚴。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Junyan.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei, courtesy name Junyan.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，鄭滑節度使盧群辟為從事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; the Military Governor of Zheng-Slip Lu Qun summoned him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and joined the staff of Lu Qun, governor of Zheng and Hua.

sentences.zh: 群卒，命戣權掌留務，監軍使以氣淩之，戣無所屈降。

translations.literal: When Qun died, he ordered Wei to provisionally handle remaining affairs; the army supervisory commissioner tried to overbear him by force of manner, but Wei in no way submitted or yielded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qun died Wei was left in charge of the circuit's affairs. The eunuch army supervisor tried to intimidate him, but Wei would not bend.

sentences.zh: 入為侍御史，累轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Attending Censor and was successively transferred among Secretariat officers.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Attending Censor and rose through various posts in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元和初，改諫議大夫，侃然忠讜，有諫臣體。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was changed to Remonstrating Adviser; upright and loyal in remonstrance, he had the bearing of a remonstrating minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was made Remonstrating Adviser—frank, loyal, and every inch the remonstrating official.

sentences.zh: 上疏論時政四條，帝意嘉納。

translations.literal: He memorialized discussing four items of current policy; the emperor's mind was pleased and he accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on four points of current policy, and the emperor received it favorably.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，內官劉希光受將軍孫璹賂二十萬貫，以求方鎮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year the inner palace official Liu Xiguang received from General Sun Guan a bribe of two hundred thousand strings of cash to seek a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year (811) the eunuch Liu Xiguang took a bribe of two hundred thousand cash strings from General Sun Guan in exchange for securing a military governorship.

sentences.zh: 事敗，賜希光死。

translations.literal: The matter was exposed and Xiguang was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light Xiguang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 時吐突承璀以出軍無功，諫官論列，坐希光事出為淮南監軍使。

translations.literal: At the time Tushi Chenghuan for leading troops without achievement was criticized by remonstrating officials; because of the Xiguang affair he was sent out as Army Supervisory Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Tushi Chenghuan, who had led troops without success, was attacked by the remonstrators; implicated in the Liu Xiguang case, he was exiled as army supervisory commissioner in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 太子通事舍人李涉知上待承璀意未衰，欲投匭上疏，論承璀有功，希光無事，久委心腹，不宜遽棄。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's Master of Ceremonies Li She, knowing the emperor's regard for Chenghuan had not waned, wished to cast a memorial box petition, arguing Chenghuan had merit, Xiguang was innocent, long entrusted as a close confidant, and should not hastily be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li She, Master of Ceremonies to the crown prince, saw that the emperor still favored Chenghuan and planned to drop a petition into the complaint box arguing that Chenghuan had served well, that Xiguang was innocent, and that a long-trusted confidant should not be cast aside so abruptly.

sentences.zh: 戣為匭使，得涉副章，不受，面詰責之。

translations.literal: Wei was commissioner of the petition box; obtaining She's duplicate petition, he did not accept it and face to face interrogated and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, as commissioner of the petition box, intercepted She's draft, refused it, and confronted him in person.

sentences.zh: 涉乃進疏於光順門。

translations.literal: She thereupon submitted the memorial at the Guangshun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: She then submitted the memorial at the Guangshun Gate instead.

sentences.zh: 戣極論其與中官交結，言甚激切。

translations.literal: Wei argued to the utmost his collusion with inner palace officials; his words were very fierce and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei denounced him in the strongest terms for colluding with the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 詔貶涉為陜州司倉。

translations.literal: An edict demoted She to Granary Officer of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banished She to the post of granary officer in Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幸臣聞之側目，人為危之。

translations.literal: Favored ministers, hearing of it, glared sidelong; men considered him in danger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites glared at him; many feared for his life.

sentences.zh: 戣高步公卿間，以方嚴見憚。

translations.literal: Wei walked tall among dukes and ministers and was feared for his upright sternness.
translations.idiomatic: Among the highest officials Wei carried himself with unbending dignity and was widely feared.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太子侍讀，遷吏部侍郎，轉左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Reader to the Crown Prince, promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel, and transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Reader to the crown prince, then Vice Minister of Personnel, then Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年，信州刺史李位為州將韋嶽讒譖於本使監軍高重謙，言位結聚術士，以圖不軌。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Prefect of Xinzhou Li Wei was slandered by the prefectural general Wei Yue to the circuit's army supervisory commissioner Gao Chongqian, saying Wei gathered and assembled Daoist masters to plot sedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (814) the prefect of Xinzhou, Li Wei, was denounced by his military adjutant Wei Yue to the eunuch supervisory commissioner Gao Chongqian, who charged that Wei had gathered Daoist ritual specialists to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 追位至京師，鞫於禁中。

translations.literal: Wei was summoned to the capital and interrogated within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was hauled to the capital and interrogated inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 戣奏曰：「刺史得罪，合歸法司按問，不合劾於內仗。」

translations.literal: Wei memorialized saying: "When a prefect is guilty, it is fitting he return to the judicial offices for investigation; it is not fitting to impeach him before the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei memorialized: "When a prefect stands accused, the case belongs in the regular courts. He should not be tried before the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 乃出付御史臺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out and handed over to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The case was thereupon turned over to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 戣與三司訊鞫，得其狀。

translations.literal: Wei with the Three Offices interrogated and obtained the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei joined the Three Offices in the investigation and established the facts.

sentences.zh: 位好黃老道，時修齋箓，與山人王恭合煉藥物，別無逆狀。

translations.literal: Wei was fond of Huang-Lao Daoism, at times performed fasting and talisman rites, and together with the mountain man Wang Gong refined medicines; apart from this there was no sign of sedition.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei practiced Huang-Lao Daoism, observed ritual fasts, and compounded medicines with the recluse Wang Gong—nothing that amounted to sedition.

sentences.zh: 以嶽誣告，決殺。

translations.literal: Because Yue falsely reported, he was decisively executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue was executed for his false accusation.

sentences.zh: 貶位建州司馬。

translations.literal: Wei was demoted to Vice Administrator of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was demoted to vice administrator of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時非戣論諫，罪在不測，人士稱之。

translations.literal: At the time, but for Wei's remonstrance, the guilt would have been beyond reckoning; scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Without Wei's intervention Li Wei might have faced an unpredictable fate; contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 愈為中官所惡，尋出為華州刺史、潼關防禦等使。

translations.literal: Wei was hated by inner palace officials; soon he went out as Prefect of Huazhou and Defense Commissioner of Tong Pass et al.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs hated him; he was soon sent out as prefect of Huazhou and defender of Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and was changed to Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as chief justice of the Court of Judicial Review, then was made Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十二年，嶺南節度使崔詠卒，三軍請帥，宰相奏擬皆不稱旨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Military Governor of Lingnan Cui Yong died; the Three Armies requested a commander; the chief ministers' memorial nominations all failed to match the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (817) the military governor of Lingnan, Cui Yong, died. The army demanded a successor, but none of the names the chief ministers proposed satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 因入對，上謂裴度曰：「嘗有上疏論南海進蚶菜者，詞甚忠正，此人何在，卿第求之。」

translations.literal: Accordingly on entering audience the emperor said to Pei Du: "There was once one who memorialized on sending oysters and vegetables from the Southern Sea; his words were very loyal and upright. Where is this man—you simply seek him out.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience the emperor told Pei Du, "Someone once memorialized against sending delicacies from the southern seas—his words were thoroughly loyal. Find that man for me.

sentences.zh: 度退訪之。

translations.literal: Du withdrew and inquired.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du withdrew and made inquiries.

sentences.zh: 或曰祭酒孔戣嘗論此事，度征疏進之。

translations.literal: Someone said Director of Education Kong Wei had once discussed this matter; Du sought out the memorial and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He was told that Kong Wei, Director of Education, had raised the issue; Pei Du retrieved the memorial and presented it.

sentences.zh: 即日授廣州刺史，兼御史大夫、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Prefect of Guangzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Wei was appointed prefect of Guangzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 戣剛正清儉，在南海，請刺史俸料之外，絕其取索。

translations.literal: Wei was upright, correct, pure, and frugal; in the Southern Sea, beyond requesting the prefect's salary provisions, he cut off all exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, austere, and frugal, he governed the south by living on his official salary alone and forbidding every form of unauthorized levy.

sentences.zh: 先是帥南海者，京師權要多托買南人為奴婢，戣不受托。

translations.literal: Previously those who governed the Southern Sea—powerful families in the capital mostly entrusted them to buy southern people as slaves and maidservants; Wei did not accept entrustments.
translations.idiomatic: Previous governors had let influential families in the capital use them as brokers to buy southerners as slaves; Wei refused every such request.

sentences.zh: 至郡，禁絕賣女口。

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery he prohibited and ended the sale of women.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he outlawed the trafficking of women.

sentences.zh: 先是準詔禱南海神，多令從事代祠。

translations.literal: Previously, according to edict to pray to the Southern Sea god, many ordered staff officers to substitute in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier governors, when ordered to perform rites to the god of the Southern Sea, usually sent subordinates in their place.

sentences.zh: 戣每受詔，自犯風波而往。

translations.literal: Whenever Wei received an edict, he personally braved wind and waves to go.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the edict came Wei went in person, braving wind and sea.

sentences.zh: 韓愈在潮州，作詩以美之。

translations.literal: Han Yu was in Chaozhou and composed a poem to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, then in exile at Chaozhou, wrote a poem in his praise.

sentences.zh: 時桂管經略使楊旻、桂仲武、裴行立等騷動生蠻，以求功伐，遂至嶺表累歲用兵。

translations.literal: At the time the Guiguan Pacification Commissioner Yang Min, Gui Zhongwu, Pei Xingli and others stirred up the native tribes seeking merit through campaigns; consequently in Lingnan there were many years of military use.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Guiguan commissioners such as Yang Min, Gui Zhongwu, and Pei Xingli provoked the tribal peoples in pursuit of military glory, keeping the Lingnan frontier at war for years.

sentences.zh: 唯戣以清儉為理，不務邀功，交、廣大理。

translations.literal: Only Wei governed through purity and frugality, did not strive to invite merit; Jiao and Guang were greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei governed by honest austerity, seeking no glory on the battlefield, and brought peace to Jiao and Guang.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne he was summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne Wei was recalled as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，或告戣在南海時家人受賂，上不之責，改右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Changqing reign period someone reported that while Wei was in the Southern Sea his family received bribes; the emperor did not blame him and changed him to Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: During Changqing someone accused his family of taking bribes while he was in the south. The emperor declined to punish him but transferred him to Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 累請老，詔以禮部尚書致仕，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement; an edict made him Minister of Rites in retirement from office, with a gracious edict praising and commending him.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated requests to retire he was permitted to leave office as Minister of Rites, with an edict warmly commending his service.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司歲致羊酒，如漢禮征士故事。

translations.literal: Moreover he ordered the relevant offices yearly to deliver sheep and wine, as in the Han rite of summoning scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered the relevant offices to send him wine and mutton each year, following the Han precedent for honoring retired scholars.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年正月卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Changqing he died, aged seventy-three at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the fourth year of Changqing (824), aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子遵孺、溫裕，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zunru and Wenyü both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zunru and Wenyu both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中已後，叠居顯職。

translations.literal: After the Dazhong reign period they repeatedly held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong era they rose repeatedly to high office.

sentences.zh: 溫裕位京兆尹、天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Wenyü reached the posts of Magistrate of the Capital Municipality and Military Governor of Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu served as magistrate of the capital district and military governor of the Tianping army.

sentences.zh: 遵孺子緯，自有傳。

translations.literal: Zunru's son Wei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zunru's son Kong Wei has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 戢，字方舉，戣母弟也。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Fangju, was the younger brother of Wei by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji, courtesy name Fangju, was Kong Wei's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 以季父巢父死難，德宗嘉其忠，詔與一子正員官，因授戢修武尉。

translations.literal: Because his father's younger brother Chaofu died in loyal service, Dezong commended his loyalty and edicted that one son receive a full regular office; accordingly Ji was appointed Sheriff of Xiuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Because his uncle Chaofu had died in loyal service, Dezong honored the family's sacrifice with an edict granting a regular post to one son; Ji was given the sheriffdom of Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 以長兄戡未仕，固乞回授。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Kan had not yet taken office, he firmly begged to transfer the grant back.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Kan had not yet taken office, he begged to transfer the appointment to him.

sentences.zh: 舉明經登第，判入高等，授秘書省校書郎、陽翟尉，入拜監察御史，轉殿中，分司東都。

translations.literal: He presented himself for the mingjing examination and passed, his judgment entered the high grade; he was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat, Sheriff of Yangzhai, entered and was appointed Investigating Censor, transferred to Palace Censor, with duty station at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination with high marks, served as proofreader in the Secretariat and sheriff of Yangzhai, then entered the capital as Investigating Censor and Palace Censor, with nominal duty in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 時昭義節度判官徐玟，以狡慝助成從史之惡。

translations.literal: At the time the Zhaoyi Military Governor's judicial reviewer Xu Min, through cunning and wickedness helped bring Congshi's evils to completion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Min, judicial reviewer under the Zhaoyi governor, had used his cunning to strengthen Lu Congshi's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 從史既得罪，孟元陽為昭義節度，復欲用玟為賓佐，戢遂牒澤潞收玟以俟命，然後列狀上聞，竟流玟播州。

translations.literal: Congshi having already been punished, Meng Yuanyang became Military Governor of Zhaoyi and again wished to employ Min as a staff member; Ji thereupon sent a dispatch to Ze-Lu to arrest Min and await orders, then arranged a memorial to report upward; in the end Min was banished to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Congshi fell, the new Zhaoyi governor Meng Yuanyang wanted to bring Xu Min back onto his staff. Ji ordered Ze and Lu to detain Min pending the court's decision, memorialized the case, and had Min exiled to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 轉侍御史、庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor and Assistant Director in the Ministry of Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor and Assistant Director in the Ministry of Treasury.

sentences.zh: 初，涇師之亂，硃泚署彭偃為舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning, during the disorder of the Jing army, Zhu Ci appointed Peng Yan as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Jingzhou army mutiny, Zhu Ci had appointed Peng Yan as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 至是偃子充符為鄜坊從事，或薦其才，執事者召至京師。

translations.literal: By this time Yan's son Chongfu served as a staff officer in Fufang; someone recommended his talent, and those in charge summoned him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By then Peng Yan's son Chongfu was on the staff of Fufang Circuit; when his abilities were recommended, the authorities summoned him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 戢謂京兆尹裴武曰：「硃泚為偽詔，指斥乘輿，皆彭偃之詞也。

translations.literal: Ji said to the Metropolitan Governor Pei Wu: "The forged edicts Zhu Ci composed, denouncing the imperial carriage—all were Peng Yan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Ji told Metropolitan Governor Pei Wu, "The forged edicts Zhu Ci issued and the passages denouncing the emperor were all written by Peng Yan.

sentences.zh: 悖逆之子，不能鳥竄獸伏，乃違道以幹譽，子盍效季孫行父之逐莒仆，以勉事君者。」

translations.literal: The son of a treasonous rebel cannot hide like a bird in its nest or a beast in its den, yet he flouts the Way to seek reputation. Why do you not follow Ji Sun Xingfu's expulsion of Ju Pu, to encourage those who serve their lord?"
translations.idiomatic: The son of a traitor ought to lie low like a fugitive bird or beast, not flout propriety to burnish his own name. You should take your cue from Jisun Xingfu, who drove out Ju Pu—a model for loyal servants everywhere.

sentences.zh: 武即日逐充符。

translations.literal: Wu that same day banished Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu banished Chongfu the very same day.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹，出為汝州刺史、大理卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Metropolitan Governor, sent out as Prefect of Ruzhou and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Metropolitan Governor, then sent out to serve as prefect of Ruzhou and chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 出為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Tanzhou and Hunan Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou and commissioner of Hunan Observation Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時兄戣為嶺南，兄弟皆居節鎮，朝野榮之。

translations.literal: At the time his elder brother Kai was in Lingnan; both brothers held frontier commands, and court and public alike honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his elder brother Kai governed in Lingnan; with both brothers holding military commands, the court and the public looked on them with pride.

sentences.zh: 入為右散騎常侍，拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and was appointed Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and was appointed Metropolitan Governor.

sentences.zh: 時累月亢旱，深軫聖情。

translations.literal: At the time drought had lasted many months, deeply troubling the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Drought had persisted for months, and the emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 戢自禱雨於曲池，是夕大雨。

translations.literal: Ji personally prayed for rain at Quchi; that evening great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ji prayed for rain at Quchi Pool himself; that very night a heavy rain fell.

sentences.zh: 文宗甚悅，詔兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong was greatly pleased and ordered him to additionally serve as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was greatly pleased and appointed him concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大和三年正月卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Dahe he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of Dahe 3 and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子溫業，登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Wenye passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenye passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中後，歷位通顯。

translations.literal: After Dazhong, he successively held prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong era he rose through a series of high offices.

sentences.zh: 溫業子晦。

translations.literal: Wenye's son was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wenye's son was Hui.

sentences.zh: 許孟容，字公範，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Xu Mengrong, courtesy name Gongfan, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mengrong, styled Gongfan, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父鳴謙，究通《易象》，官至撫州刺史，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Mingqian thoroughly mastered the Images of the Changes, reached the office of Prefect of Fuzhou, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mingqian had mastered the Images of the Changes, rose to prefect of Fuzhou, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孟容少以文詞知名，舉進士甲科，後究《王氏易》登科，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Mengrong from youth was famous for literary skill; he passed the jinshi in the top grade, later mastered Wang Bi's Changes and passed that examination, and was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong won early renown for his literary gifts. He passed the jinshi in the top grade, later took and passed the examination in Wang Bi's Commentary on the Changes, and was appointed a proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙贊為荊、襄等道黜陟使，表為判官。

translations.literal: Zhao Zan served as Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioner for the Jing and Xiang circuits and recommended him as judicial reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zan was Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioner for the Jing and Xiang circuits, he recommended Mengrong as his judicial reviewer.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，徐州節度使張建封辟為從事，四遷侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, the Military Governor of Xuzhou Zhang Jianfeng recruited him as a staff officer; after four promotions he became Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, Zhang Jianfeng, military governor of Xuzhou, brought him onto his staff; after four promotions he became Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 李納屯兵境上，揚言入寇。

translations.literal: Li Na encamped troops on the border and proclaimed that he would invade.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na massed troops on the border and threatened invasion.

sentences.zh: 建封遣將吏數輩告諭，不聽。

translations.literal: Jianfeng sent several officers and officials to instruct him, but Li Na would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng sent several officers and officials to reason with him, but Li Na refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 於是遣孟容單車詣納，為陳逆順禍福之計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Mengrong alone in a single carriage to Li Na to set forth the calculus of treason and loyalty, fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then sent Mengrong alone in a single carriage to Li Na to explain the consequences of rebellion and loyalty, of ruin and reward.

sentences.zh: 納即日發使追兵，因請修好。

translations.literal: Na that same day dispatched envoys to recall his troops and requested restored amity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na that same day sent envoys to recall his troops and asked to restore friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 遂表孟容為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Jianfeng then memorialized to appoint Mengrong Prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then memorialized the court to appoint Mengrong prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 無幾，德宗知其才，征為禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long Dezong knew his talent and summoned him as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Dezong recognized his ability and summoned him to serve as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有公主之子，請補弘文、崇文館諸生，孟容舉令式不許。

translations.literal: There was a princess's son who requested appointment as a student in the Hongwen and Chongwen Halls; Mengrong cited the regulations and refused.
translations.idiomatic: When a princess's son asked to be enrolled as a student in the Hongwen and Chongwen halls, Mengrong cited the regulations and refused.

sentences.zh: 主訴於上，命中使問狀。

translations.literal: The princess complained to the emperor, who ordered a palace envoy to inquire into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The princess appealed to the emperor, who sent a palace envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 孟容執奏，竟得遷本曹郎中。

translations.literal: Mengrong held firm in his memorial and in the end was transferred to Director of his own bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong stood by his memorial and was eventually promoted to Director within his own ministry.

sentences.zh: 德宗降誕日，禦麟德殿，命孟容等登座，與釋、老之徒講論。

translations.literal: On Dezong's birthday he attended at Qinde Hall, ordered Mengrong and others to take seats, and debated with Buddhist and Daoist practitioners.
translations.idiomatic: On Dezong's birthday the emperor held court at Qinde Hall, seated Mengrong and others, and joined them in debate with Buddhist and Daoist masters.

sentences.zh: 十四年，轉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a year later he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 十七年夏，好畤縣風雹傷麥，上命品官覆視，不實，詔罰京兆尹顧少連已下。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventeenth year a wind-and-hail storm in Haozhi County damaged the wheat crop; the emperor ordered ranked officials to reinspect; the report proved inaccurate, and an edict punished Metropolitan Governor Gu Shaolian and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenyuan 17 a hailstorm damaged the wheat crop in Haozhi County. The emperor ordered ranked officials to verify the damage, found the report inaccurate, and issued an edict punishing Metropolitan Governor Gu Shaolian and his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 敕出，孟容執奏曰：「府縣上事不實，罪止奪俸停官，其於弘宥，已是殊澤。

translations.literal: When the edict issued, Mengrong held it and memorialized: "When prefectures and counties report inaccurately, the penalty is merely confiscation of salary and suspension from office; in showing great clemency, this is already exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Mengrong held it back and memorialized: "When prefectural and county officials submit inaccurate reports, the proper penalty is confiscation of salary and suspension from office. To show mercy even in that case is already an extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 但陛下使品官覆視後，更擇憲官一人，再令驗察，覆視轉審，隱欺益明。

translations.literal: But after Your Majesty has ranked officials reinspect, if you further select one censorial official and again order verification—reinspection yielding further examination—concealment and deceit would become all the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: But after Your Majesty sends ranked officials to reinspect, if you then choose one censorial official and order a second verification—each review uncovering more—the concealment and deceit would become all the clearer.

sentences.zh: 事宜觀聽，法歸綱紀。

translations.literal: Matters ought to be visible to sight and hearing; law returns to discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs should be open to public scrutiny, and the law should uphold proper order.

sentences.zh: 臣受官中謝日，伏請詔敕有須詳議者，則乞停留晷刻，得以奏陳。

translations.literal: On the day I received office and gave thanks at court, I humbly requested that when edicts require detailed deliberation, I might ask them held briefly so I could memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: On the day I took office and gave thanks at court, I humbly asked that whenever an edict required careful deliberation, it be held briefly so that I might submit a memorial.

sentences.zh: 此敕既非急，宣可以少駐。」

translations.literal: This edict is not urgent; its promulgation could pause a little."
translations.idiomatic: This edict is not urgent; its promulgation could wait a little.

sentences.zh: 詔雖不許，公議是之。

translations.literal: Although the edict was not granted, public opinion sided with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his request, but public opinion sided with Mengrong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，浙江東道觀察使裴肅卒，以攝副使齊總為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Zhejiang East Circuit Observation Commissioner Pei Su died, and Acting Vice Commissioner Qi Zong was made Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 18 the Zhejiang East observation commissioner Pei Su died, and acting vice commissioner Qi Zong was appointed prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 時總為肅剝下進奉以希恩，遽授大郡，物議喧然。

translations.literal: At the time Zong, on Su's behalf, had squeezed the people for tribute to the court seeking favor; suddenly granted a great prefecture, public criticism was loud.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zong had been squeezing the people under Pei Su for tribute to the court in hopes of imperial favor; when he was suddenly given a major prefecture, public criticism erupted.

sentences.zh: 詔出，孟容執奏曰：「陛下比者以兵戎之地，或有不獲已超授者。

translations.literal: When the edict issued, Mengrong held it and memorialized: "Your Majesty lately, in regions of military conflict, has sometimes had no choice but to grant extraordinary promotions.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Mengrong held it back and memorialized: "Your Majesty has lately, in regions torn by war, sometimes had no choice but to grant extraordinary promotions.

sentences.zh: 今衢州無他虞，齊總無殊績，忽此超授，群情驚駭。

translations.literal: Now Quzhou has no other concerns; Qi Zong has no special merit; this sudden extraordinary appointment alarms everyone.
translations.idiomatic: But Quzhou faces no special threat, and Qi Zong has no outstanding achievements. This sudden extraordinary appointment has alarmed everyone.

sentences.zh: 總是浙東判官，今詔敕稱權知留後，攝都團練副使，向來無此敕命。

translations.literal: Zong is merely a judicial reviewer of Zhedong; now the edict calls him Acting Commissioner and Acting Deputy Military Training Commissioner—there has never been such an order before.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zong is only a judicial reviewer in Zhedong, yet the edict names him acting commissioner and acting deputy military training commissioner—an appointment without precedent.

sentences.zh: 便用此詔，尤恐不可。

translations.literal: To use this edict as written, I especially fear it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: To issue this edict as written would, I fear, be wholly unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 若總必有可錄，陛下須要酬勞，即明書課最，超一兩資與改。

translations.literal: If Zong truly has accomplishments worth recording and Your Majesty must reward him, then clearly write out his evaluation and advance him one or two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: If Qi Zong truly deserves reward, Your Majesty should set out his merits in plain terms and advance him one or two ranks accordingly.

sentences.zh: 今舉朝之人，不知總之功能，衢州浙東大郡，總自大理評事兼監察御史授之，使遐邇不甘，兇惡騰口。

translations.literal: Now everyone at court does not know Zong's capabilities; Quzhou is a great prefecture of Zhedong; appointing him from Grand Court of Review clerk concurrent Investigating Censor makes near and far resentful and lets the wicked loose their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court knows nothing of Qi Zong's abilities, yet Quzhou is one of Zhedong's great prefectures. To appoint him from the lowly post of clerk in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Investigating Censor will breed resentment near and far and give the wicked room to speak.

sentences.zh: 如臣言不切，乞陛下暫停此詔，密使人聽察，必賀聖朝無私。

translations.literal: If my words are not to the point, I beg Your Majesty temporarily withhold this edict and secretly send someone to listen and observe—they will surely celebrate the holy court's lack of favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: If my words miss the mark, I beg Your Majesty to withhold this edict for now and secretly send someone to listen to public opinion—you will surely be hailed for a court without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 今齊總詔謹隨狀封進。」

translations.literal: Herewith I respectfully enclose Qi Zong's edict with this memorial."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully enclose Qi Zong's edict with this memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋有諫官論列，乃留中不下。

translations.literal: Soon remonstrating officials also petitioned, and the edict was held at court and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials soon joined in, and the edict was held at court and never issued.

sentences.zh: 德宗召孟容對於延英，諭之曰：「使百執事皆如卿，朕何憂也。」

translations.literal: Dezong summoned Mengrong to audience at Yanying and instructed him: "If every official were like you, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned Mengrong to an audience at Yanying Hall and told him, "If every official were like you, what would I have to worry about?

sentences.zh: 自給事中袁高論盧杞後，未嘗有可否，及聞孟容之奏，四方皆感上之聽納，嘉孟容之當官。

translations.literal: Since Supervising Secretary Yuan Gao's remonstrance regarding Lu Qi, there had never again been approval or rejection of such holds; when Mengrong's memorial was heard, all directions were moved by the emperor's willingness to listen and praised Mengrong's fulfillment of office.
translations.idiomatic: Since Supervising Secretary Yuan Gao's remonstrance against Lu Qi, no such hold had ever been granted or denied; when Mengrong's memorial was heard, people everywhere were moved by the emperor's willingness to listen and praised Mengrong for doing his duty.

sentences.zh: 十九年夏旱，孟容上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the summer drought of the nineteenth year, Mengrong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the summer drought of Zhenyuan 19, Mengrong submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣伏聞陛下數月已來，齋居損膳，為兆庶心疲，又敕有司，走於群望，牲於百神，而密雲不雨，首種未入。

translations.literal: I have heard that Your Majesty for many months now has lived in purification and reduced meals, exhausting your heart on behalf of the masses; moreover you have ordered the offices to rush to all sacred sites and offer victims to the hundred spirits—yet dense clouds do not rain and the first sowing has not entered.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that for many months now Your Majesty has lived in abstinence and reduced your meals, wearing yourself out for the sake of the people; that you have ordered officials to hurry to every sacred site and offer sacrifices to the hundred spirits—yet the clouds gather without rain, and the first planting has not gone in.

sentences.zh: 豈觴醪有闕，祈祝非誠，為陰陽適然，豐歉前定，何聖意精至，甘澤未答也？

translations.literal: Is it that sacrificial wine was lacking or prayers were not sincere—or that yin and yang simply ran their course and plenty and want were preordained? Why, when the sage intent reached such refinement, has sweet moisture not answered?
translations.idiomatic: Was the sacrificial wine insufficient, or the prayers insincere? Was it simply that yin and yang ran their course and plenty and famine were fated? Why, when Your Majesty's devotion has been so earnest, has the sweet rain not come in reply?

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀自古天人交感事，未有不由百姓利病之急者、切者，邦家教令之大者、遠者。

translations.literal: I have surveyed affairs of mutual resonance between Heaven and man from antiquity; never have there been cases not rooted in what is urgent and pressing in the people's weal and woe—great and far-reaching policies of state and family teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In every case I have examined of Heaven and man responding to one another, the cause has always lain in what most urgently affects the people's welfare—in the great and far-reaching policies by which a state is governed.

sentences.zh: 京師是萬國所會，強幹弱枝，自古通規。

translations.literal: The capital is where the myriad states converge; strong trunk, weak branches—an ancient constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is where all the realm gathers; strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches has been the rule since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其一年稅錢及地租，出入一百萬貫。

translations.literal: Its yearly tax money and land rent amount to over one million strings in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Its annual tax levies and land rents come to more than one million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 臣伏冀陛下即日下令，全放免之；

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will this very day issue orders to remit them entirely;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to issue an order this very day remitting them entirely;

sentences.zh: 其次，三分放二。

translations.literal: next best, remit two-thirds of three parts.
translations.idiomatic: or, failing that, remit two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 且使旱涸之際，免更流亡。

translations.literal: Thus in this time of drought and desiccation, prevent further flight of the people.
translations.idiomatic: That way, in this season of drought and desolation, the people may be spared further flight from their homes.

sentences.zh: 若播種無望，征斂如舊，則必愁怨遷徙，不顧墳墓矣。

translations.literal: If sowing is hopeless yet levies continue as before, they will surely fret, resent, and migrate without regard even for ancestral graves.
translations.idiomatic: If planting is hopeless yet the levies continue as before, the people will surely grow bitter, resentful, and displaced—even abandoning their ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為德音一發，膏澤立應，變災為福，期在斯須。

translations.literal: This fool thinks that once a decree of virtue issues, nourishing rain will immediately respond—turning disaster to blessing, expected in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that once a decree of grace is issued, nourishing rain will answer at once—disaster turned to blessing in a moment.

sentences.zh: 戶部所收掌錢，非度支歲計，本防緩急別用。

translations.literal: Funds held by the Ministry of Revenue are not part of the yearly budget of the Department of Public Works; originally set aside for separate emergency use.
translations.idiomatic: The funds held by the Ministry of Revenue are not part of the Department of Public Works' annual budget; they were originally set aside for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 今此炎旱，直支一百余萬貫，代京兆百姓一年差科，實陛下巍巍睿謀，天下鼓舞歌揚者也。

translations.literal: Now in this scorching drought, to expend directly over one million strings in place of the capital people's yearly corvée and levies—truly this would be Your Majesty's towering wisdom, and all under Heaven would thrill and sing praise.
translations.idiomatic: In this scorching drought, to spend more than one million strings to relieve the capital people of a year's corvée and levies would be an act of towering wisdom—and all under Heaven would rejoice and sing Your Majesty's praise.

sentences.zh: 復更省察庶政之中，有流移征防，當還而未還者，徒役禁錮，當釋而未釋者，逋懸饋送，當免而未免者，沈滯郁抑，當伸而未伸者，有一於此，則特降明命，令有司條列，三日內聞奏。

translations.literal: Further examine among all governance: those on frontier service who should return but have not; corvée laborers and prisoners who should be released but have not; overdue tribute and deliveries that should be remitted but were not; cases sunk in delay and suppressed grievance that should be righted but were not—if any of these exists, then specially descend a clear command ordering the offices to itemize and report within three days.
translations.idiomatic: Further examine the whole of government: soldiers on frontier duty who should be sent home but have not been; corvée laborers and prisoners who should be released but remain confined; overdue tribute and deliveries that should be remitted but have not been; grievances long suppressed that should be redressed but have not been. If any of these exist, issue a special clear command ordering the relevant offices to itemize them and report within three days.

sentences.zh: 其當還、當釋、當免、當伸者，下詔之日，所在即時施行。

translations.literal: For those who should return, be released, be remitted, or be righted—on the day the edict descends, wherever they are, carry it out at once.
translations.idiomatic: For all who should return, be released, be remitted, or be redressed—wherever they are, the order should take effect the very day the edict is issued.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為如此而神不監，歲不稔，古未之有。

translations.literal: This fool believes that if it were done thus and the spirits still did not oversee or the year still did not ripen, there would be no precedent in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that if all this were done and the spirits still did not look down in favor, and the year still did not yield a harvest, it would be without precedent in all antiquity.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，物議嘉之。

translations.literal: Though the proposal was not adopted, public opinion praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the proposal was not adopted, public opinion praised it.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，坐裴延齡、李齊運等讒謗流貶者，動十數年不量移，故因旱歉，孟容奏此以諷。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan, those banished on slander by Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and others often went ten-plus years without compassionate relocation; therefore amid drought and poor harvest Mengrong memorialized this as indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, those exiled on the slander of Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and others often went more than ten years without compassionate relocation; amid drought and famine Mengrong submitted this memorial as an indirect admonition.

sentences.zh: 然終貞元世，罕有遷移者。

translations.literal: Yet through all the Zhenyuan era, relocations were rare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet throughout the Zhenyuan era, such relocations remained rare.

sentences.zh: 孟容以諷諭太切，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: Mengrong, because his indirect admonition was too sharp, was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Because his indirect admonition had cut too close, Mengrong was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷刑部侍郎、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜京兆尹，賜紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Metropolitan Governor and granted the purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 4 he was appointed Metropolitan Governor and granted the purple robe of high rank.

sentences.zh: 神策吏李昱假貸長安富人錢八千貫，滿三歲不償。

translations.literal: A Shence Army clerk named Li Yu borrowed eight thousand strings from a wealthy Chang'an man; three years passed without repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, a clerk in the Shence Army, borrowed eight thousand strings of cash from a wealthy Chang'an merchant and failed to repay it for three years.

sentences.zh: 孟容遣吏收捕械系，克日命還之，曰：「不及期當死。」

translations.literal: Mengrong sent officers to arrest and fetter him, set a deadline for repayment, and said: "If the deadline is not met, he dies."
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong sent officers to arrest and imprison him, set a deadline for repayment, and declared: "If he misses the deadline, he dies.

sentences.zh: 自興元已後，禁軍有功，又中貴之尤有渥恩者，方得護軍。

translations.literal: Since after Xingyuan, only those with merit in the palace armies—and especially eunuchs with special imperial favor—could protect soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Since after Xingyuan, only palace soldiers with distinguished service—and above all those backed by favored eunuchs—could shield their men from the law.

sentences.zh: 故軍士日益縱橫，府縣不能制。

translations.literal: Therefore soldiers daily grew more unrestrained, and prefectures and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the soldiers grew daily more lawless, and the prefectural and county authorities could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 孟容剛正不懼，以法繩之，一軍盡驚，冤訴於上。

translations.literal: Mengrong, upright and fearless, bound them by law; the whole army was alarmed and pleaded injustice to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong, upright and unafraid, held them to the law. The whole army was shaken and appealed to the emperor that an injustice had been done.

sentences.zh: 立命中使宣旨，令送本軍，孟容系之不遣。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict was sent via palace envoy ordering him returned to his army; Mengrong kept him shackled and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately sent a palace envoy with an edict ordering Li Yu returned to his unit, but Mengrong kept him in chains and refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 中使再至，乃執奏曰：「臣誠知不奉詔當誅，然臣職司輦轂，合為陛下彈抑豪強。

translations.literal: When the envoy came again, he held firm and memorialized: "I truly know disobeying an edict merits death; yet my duty governs the imperial carriage-region—I ought to restrain the powerful on Your Majesty's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came a second time, Mengrong held his ground and memorialized: "I know full well that disobeying an edict is punishable by death; yet my office governs the capital region—it is my duty to restrain the powerful on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 錢未盡輸，昱不可得。」

translations.literal: Until the money is fully paid, Yu cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Until the debt is fully paid, Li Yu cannot be released.

sentences.zh: 上以其守正，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing his integrity, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, respecting his integrity, allowed it.

sentences.zh: 自此豪右斂跡，威望大震。

translations.literal: From this the powerful curbed their steps, and his authority greatly shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the powerful curbed their behavior, and his authority resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官權知禮部貢舉，頗抑浮華，選擇才藝。

translations.literal: Soon with that rank he acted as head of the Ministry of Rites examinations; he greatly suppressed flashy style and selected talent and skill.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served concurrently as head of the Ministry of Rites examinations, where he strongly discouraged flashy writing and selected candidates for genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹，亦有威名。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Henan Metropolitan Governor and also had a formidable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as metropolitan governor of Henan, where he likewise earned a formidable reputation.

sentences.zh: 俄知禮部選事，征拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he directed Ministry of Rites selections and was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took charge of Ministry of Rites selections and was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會十年六月，盜殺宰相武元衡，並傷議臣裴度。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year, assassins killed Chancellor Wu Yuanheng and also wounded remonstrating official Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yuanhe 10, assassins killed Chancellor Wu Yuanheng and wounded the remonstrating official Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 時淮夷逆命，兇威方熾，王師問罪，未有成功。

translations.literal: At the time the Huaiyi rebelled; ferocious power blazed; the imperial army sought punishment without success yet.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Huai rebels were in revolt, their violence at its height, and the imperial campaign against them had not yet succeeded.

sentences.zh: 言事者繼上章疏請罷兵。

translations.literal: Memorialists continually submitted petitions asking to cease military action.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists one after another submitted petitions calling for the army to be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 是時盜賊竊發，人情甚惑，獨孟容詣中書雪涕而言曰：「昔漢廷有一汲黯，奸臣尚為寢謀。

translations.literal: At this time bandits arose secretly; popular sentiment was greatly confused; Mengrong alone went to the Secretariat, weeping as he spoke: "Formerly the Han court had one Ji An—and treacherous ministers still laid their schemes to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were striking everywhere and public sentiment was in turmoil. Mengrong alone went to the Secretariat, tears streaming down his face, and said: "In the Han court there was but one Ji An, and even treacherous ministers were forced to abandon their schemes.

sentences.zh: 今主上英明，朝廷未有過失，而狂賊敢爾無狀，寧謂國無人乎？

translations.literal: Now our sovereign is enlightened and the court has no fault, yet mad assassins dare such lawless acts—are we to say the state has no men?
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is enlightened and the court has done no wrong, yet these mad assassins dare such outrage—are we to say the empire has no worthy men?

sentences.zh: 然轉禍為福，此其時也。

translations.literal: Yet to turn calamity to fortune—this is the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to turn calamity into fortune—this is the moment.

sentences.zh: 莫若上聞，起裴中丞為相，令主兵柄，大索賊黨，窮其奸源。」

translations.literal: Best report upward: raise Vice Censor Pei to chancellor, give him military authority, hunt widely for the assassin faction, and exhaust their treacherous source."
translations.idiomatic: The best course is to report to the throne: appoint Vice Censor Pei as chancellor, put the military command in his hands, hunt down the assassins' faction, and trace the conspiracy to its root.

sentences.zh: 後數日，度果為相，而下詔行誅。

translations.literal: Several days later Du indeed became chancellor, and an edict was issued to carry out executions.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Pei Du was indeed made chancellor, and an edict was issued ordering the pursuit and execution of the conspirators.

sentences.zh: 時孟容議論人物，有大臣風彩。

translations.literal: At the time Mengrong in discussing people had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mengrong's judgments of men and affairs had the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 由太常卿為尚書左丞，奉詔宣慰汴宋陳許河陽行營諸軍，俄拜東都留守。

translations.literal: From Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; he received an edict to declare consolation to the armies of the Bian-Song, Chen-Xu, and Heyang campaigning circuits, and soon was appointed Eastern Capital Garrison Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, received an edict to proclaim imperial consolation to the armies of the Bian-Song, Chen-Xu, and Heyang campaigning circuits, and was soon appointed commissioner of the Eastern Capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年四月卒，年七十六，贈太子少保，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he died, aged seventy-six; posthumously granted Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, at the age of seventy-six. He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 孟容方勁，富有文學。

translations.literal: Mengrong was upright and forceful, richly endowed with literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Mengrong was upright and resolute, and richly accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 其折衷禮法，考詳訓典，甚堅正，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: In mediating ritual and law and examining canonical texts in detail, he was most firm and upright, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In weighing ritual against law and scrutinizing canonical texts, he was notably firm and principled, and commentators spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 而又好推轂，樂善拔士，士多歸之。

translations.literal: Moreover he loved to push the chariot wheel, delighted in doing good and elevating scholars, and scholars mostly rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved to promote others, took pleasure in doing good and raising up men of talent, and scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 呂元膺，字景夫，鄆州東平人。

translations.literal: Lü Yuanying, courtesy name Jingfu, was a native of Dongping in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuanying, whose courtesy name was Jingfu, came from Dongping in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖紹宗，右拾遺。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shaozong was Right Remonstrance Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shaozong served as Right Remonstrance Clerk.

sentences.zh: 祖霈，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pei was Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pei served as Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 父長卿，右衛倉曹參軍，以元膺贈秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Changqing was Army Adjutant of the Right Guard Storehouse Bureau; because of Yuanying he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Changqing had been Army Adjutant of the Right Guard Storehouse Bureau; on Yuanying's account he was posthumously granted the title of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元膺質度瑰偉，有公侯之器。

translations.literal: Yuanying's bearing and stature were magnificent; he had the makings of a duke or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying was imposing in bearing and stature, and showed the makings of a great noble.

sentences.zh: 建中初，策賢良對問第，授同州安邑尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he placed in the examination on virtuous talent and policy questions, and was appointed Wei of Anyi in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianzhong era he passed the imperial examination on virtuous talent and policy questions and was appointed magistrate of Anyi in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 同州刺史侯鐈聞其名，辟為長春宮判官。

translations.literal: Tongzhou Prefect Hou Qiao heard his fame and recruited him as Recorder of Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Qiao, prefect of Tong Prefecture, heard of his reputation and recruited him as recorder of Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 屬浦賊侵軼，鐈失所，元膺遂潛跡不務進取。

translations.literal: When Pu bandits raided, Qiao lost his post, and Yuanying thereupon lived in concealment and did not strive for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits from Pu raided the region, Qiao lost his position, and Yuanying withdrew from public life and made no effort to advance his career.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，論惟明節制渭北，延在賓席，自是名達於朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan Lun Weiming controlled the north of Wei; he kept Yuanying at his guest seats, and from then his name reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era Lun Weiming held military command north of the Wei River and kept Yuanying among his honored guests; from that time his name became known at court.

sentences.zh: 惟明卒，王棲曜代領其鎮。

translations.literal: When Weiming died, Wang Qiyao took over command of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Weiming died, Wang Qiyao succeeded him in command of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 德宗俾棲曜留署使職，咨以軍政。

translations.literal: Dezong had Qiyao retain the commissioner post in his name and consulted him on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had Qiyao continue to hold the commissioner's post in his name and consulted him on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 累轉殿中侍御史，征入，真拜本官，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Palace Attending Censor, was summoned in, received formal appointment to that office, and was transferred to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Palace Attending Censor, was summoned to the capital, received formal appointment to that office, and was then transferred to the post of censor.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，服闋，除右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his stepmother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Vice Director in the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After entering mourning for his stepmother and completing the mourning period, he was appointed Vice Director in the Right Bureau of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為蘄州刺史，頗著恩信。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Qizhou and showed considerable grace and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Qi Prefecture, where he won a strong reputation for kindness and trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 嘗歲終閱郡獄囚，囚有自告者曰：「某有父母在，明日元正不得相見。」

translations.literal: Once at year's end he reviewed the prisoners in the prefectural jail; a prisoner volunteered and said: "I have parents living; tomorrow on New Year's Day I cannot see them."
translations.idiomatic: Once, at the end of the year, he reviewed the prisoners held in the prefectural jail. One prisoner stepped forward and said, "I still have parents at home, and tomorrow, on New Year's Day, I will not be able to see them.

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept.
translations.idiomatic: With that he burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 元膺憫焉，盡脫其械縱之，與為期。

translations.literal: Yuanying took pity on him, removed all his fetters and released him, setting a date for return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying was moved with pity, removed all his shackles, and released him on his word to return by an agreed date.

sentences.zh: 守吏曰：「賊不可縱。」

translations.literal: The jail keeper said: "Bandits must not be released."
translations.idiomatic: The jail keeper said, "You cannot release a bandit.

sentences.zh: 元膺曰：「吾以忠信待之。」

translations.literal: Yuanying said: "I will treat him with loyalty and trust."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying replied, "I will treat him with loyalty and good faith.

sentences.zh: 及期，無後到者。

translations.literal: When the date came, none failed to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed day arrived, not one of them failed to return.

sentences.zh: 由是群盜感義，相引而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits as a group were moved by righteousness and led one another away.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his integrity, the bandits as a group left the region, one after another.

sentences.zh: 元和初，征拜右司郎中、兼侍御史，知雜事，遷諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned and appointed Director in the Right Bureau, concurrently Censor, with charge of miscellaneous matters; he was promoted to Remonstrance Adviser and Attendant at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he was summoned and appointed Director in the Right Bureau, concurrently serving as censor with charge of miscellaneous business, and was later promoted to Remonstrance Adviser and Attendant at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 規諫駁議，大舉其職。

translations.literal: In remonstrance, admonition, and rebuttal of proposals he fully performed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In remonstrance, admonition, and review of memorials he fully discharged his office.

sentences.zh: 及鎮州王承宗之叛，憲宗將以吐突丞璀為招討處置使。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou rebelled, Xianzong was about to appoint Tu Tu Chengcui Pacification and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong of Zhen Prefecture rebelled, Emperor Xianzong intended to appoint Tu Tu Chengcui as Pacification and Disposition Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元膺與給事中穆質、孟簡，兵部侍郎許孟容等八人抗論不可，且曰：「承璀雖貴寵，然內臣也。

translations.literal: Yuanying, together with Attendants Muzhi and Meng Jian, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and five others—eight men in all—argued against it and said: "Chengcui, though honored and favored, is an inner official.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying, together with Attendants Muzhi and Meng Jian, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and five others—eight men in all—argued strenuously against the appointment, saying, "Chengcui may be honored and favored, but he is a eunuch official.

sentences.zh: 若為帥總兵，恐不為諸將所伏。」

translations.literal: If made commander-in-chief over the army, I fear the generals will not submit to him."
translations.idiomatic: If he is made commander-in-chief, I fear the generals will not accept his authority.

sentences.zh: 指諭明切，憲宗納之，為改使號，然猶專戎柄，無功而還。

translations.literal: Their arguments were pointed and clear; Xianzong accepted them and changed the commissioner's title, yet Chengcui still held sole military authority and returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Their arguments were pointed and forceful. Xianzong accepted them and changed the commissioner's title, but Chengcui still retained sole control of the army and returned without success.

sentences.zh: 出為同州刺史，及中謝，上問時政得失，元膺論奏，辭氣激切，上嘉之。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Tongzhou; at his audience of thanks the emperor asked about the gains and losses of current policy, and Yuanying presented his views in language fierce and urgent; the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Tong Prefecture. At his audience of thanks the emperor asked about the strengths and failings of current policy, and Yuanying spoke with fierce urgency. The emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 翌日謂宰相曰：「元膺有讜言直氣，宜留在左右，使言得失，卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: The next day he said to the chancellors: "Yuanying has forthright words and upright spirit; he should be kept at my side so that he may speak of gains and losses—what do you think?"
