translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor said to the chancellors, "Yuanying speaks with blunt honesty and upright spirit. He should be kept at my side to speak freely of what is right and wrong. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 李籓、裴垍賀曰：「陛下納諫，超冠百王，乃宗社無疆之休。

translations.literal: Li Fan and Pei Ji congratulated him, saying: "Your Majesty accepts remonstrance, surpassing the hundred kings—this is boundless blessing for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan and Pei Ji congratulated him, saying, "Your Majesty's willingness to accept remonstrance surpasses that of the hundred kings of antiquity. This is boundless good fortune for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 臣等不能廣求端士，又不能數進忠言，孤負聖心，合當罪戾。

translations.literal: We your ministers have been unable to seek widely for upright men, nor able frequently to advance loyal words; we have failed your sacred intent and deserve punishment.
translations.idiomatic: We have failed to seek out worthy men broadly, and we have not offered loyal counsel often enough. We have betrayed Your Majesty's trust and deserve punishment.

sentences.zh: 請留元膺給事左右。」

translations.literal: We ask that Yuanying be kept as Attendant at Your Majesty's side."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Yuanying be kept at Your Majesty's side as Attendant at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋兼皇太子侍讀，賜以金紫。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Lecturer to the Heir Apparent and granted gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Lecturer to the Heir Apparent and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 尋拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除鄂嶽觀察使，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Observation Commissioner of E-Yue; he entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Observation Commissioner of E and Yue, then recalled to the capital as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 度支使潘孟陽與太府卿王遂叠相奏論，孟陽除散騎常侍，遂為鄧州刺史，皆假以美詞。

translations.literal: Revenue Commissioner Pan Mengyang and Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary Wang Sui repeatedly submitted memorials attacking each other; Mengyang was appointed Irregular Grand Master, Sui was made Prefect of Dengzhou, and both were given flattering language.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Commissioner Pan Mengyang and Director of the Court of the Imperial Granary Wang Sui repeatedly submitted memorials attacking each other. Mengyang was appointed Irregular Grand Master and Sui was made prefect of Deng Prefecture, both appointments couched in flattering language.

sentences.zh: 元膺封還詔書，請明示枉直。

translations.literal: Yuanying sealed and returned the edict, asking that right and wrong be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying sealed and returned the edict, asking that the rights and wrongs of the case be made clear.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使裴堪奏虔州刺史李將順贓狀，朝廷不覆按，遽貶將順道州司戶。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Pei Kan memorialized the corrupt conduct of Qianzhou Prefect Li Jiangshun; the court did not reinvestigate and abruptly demoted Jiangshun to Registrar of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Pei Kan memorialized the corrupt conduct of Qian Prefecture's prefect Li Jiangshun. The court did not reinvestigate the case and abruptly demoted Jiangshun to registrar of Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元膺曰：「廉使奏刺史贓罪，不覆檢即謫去，縱堪之詞足信，亦不可為天下法。」

translations.literal: Yuanying said: "When an integrity commissioner reports a prefect's corruption, to banish him without reinvestigation—even if Kan's words are fully credible—cannot serve as law for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying said, "When an integrity commissioner reports a prefect's corruption, to exile him without reinvestigation—even if Pei Kan's account is fully credible—cannot be made a precedent for the empire.

sentences.zh: 又封詔書，請發御史按問，宰臣不能奪。

translations.literal: Again he sealed the edict and asked that censors be dispatched to investigate; the chancellors could not overrule him.
translations.idiomatic: Again he sealed and returned the edict and asked that censors be dispatched to investigate. The chancellors could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 代權德輿為東都留守、檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、都畿防禦使。

translations.literal: He replaced Quan Deyu as Eastern Capital Garrison Commissioner, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and Metropolitan Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Quan Deyu as commissioner of the Eastern Capital garrison, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and commissioner for the defense of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 舊例，留守賜旗甲，與方鎮同。

translations.literal: By old precedent the garrison commissioner was granted banners and armor, the same as a regional command.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding precedent the Eastern Capital garrison commissioner was granted military banners and armor, the same as a regional military governor.

sentences.zh: 及元膺受任不賜，朝論以淮西用兵，特用元膺守洛，不宜削其儀制，以沮威望，諫官論列，援華、汝、壽三州例。

translations.literal: When Yuanying received appointment he was not granted them; court opinion held that because troops were being used in Huaixi, Yuanying had been specially chosen to guard Luoyang and his ceremonial insignia should not be cut back to dampen his authority; remonstrance officials argued in sequence, citing the precedents of Hua, Ru, and Shou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanying took up his post, however, he was not granted them. Court opinion held that because the empire was waging war in Huaixi, Yuanying had been specially chosen to guard Luoyang and that his ceremonial insignia should not be reduced, lest his authority be undermined. Remonstrance officials argued the point at length, citing the precedents of Hua, Ru, and Shou prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此數處並宜不賜。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These several posts alike should not be granted them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "None of these posts should receive them.

sentences.zh: 留守不賜旗甲，自元膺始。

translations.literal: That garrison commissioners were not granted banners and armor began with Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of withholding banners and armor from Eastern Capital garrison commissioners began with Yuanying.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，鄆州李師道留邸伏甲謀亂。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, Li Shidao of Yanzhou stationed hidden armor in his Luoyang residence to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year of Yuanhe, Li Shidao of Yan Prefecture hid armed men in his Luoyang residence to plot an uprising.

sentences.zh: 初，師道於東都置邸院，兵諜雜以往來，吏不敢辨。

translations.literal: Earlier Shidao had established a residence compound in the Eastern Capital; soldiers and spies mingled in coming and going, and officials did not dare investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shidao had established a residence compound in the Eastern Capital through which soldiers and spies passed freely, and local officials did not dare question them.

sentences.zh: 因吳元濟北犯，郊畿多警，防禦兵盡戍伊闕。

translations.literal: Because Wu Yuanji raided northward, the capital suburbs were much alarmed, and defense troops were all garrisoned at Yique.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji launched his northern offensive, the suburbs around the capital were thrown into alarm, and all the defense troops were posted at Yique.

sentences.zh: 師道伏甲百余於邸院，將焚宮室而肆殺掠。

translations.literal: Shidao hid more than a hundred armed men in the residence compound, intending to burn the palace halls and carry out slaughter and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao concealed more than a hundred armed men in the compound, intending to burn the palace halls and unleash slaughter and plunder.

sentences.zh: 已烹牛饗眾，明日將出。

translations.literal: They had already cooked oxen to feast the host; the next day they were to sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: They had already slaughtered oxen to feast the men and planned to strike the following day.

sentences.zh: 會小將李再興告變，元膺追兵伊闕，圍之，半月無敢進攻者。

translations.literal: It happened that junior officer Li Zaixing reported the plot; Yuanying pursued with troops to Yique and besieged them; for half a month none dared press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Then junior officer Li Zaixing reported the plot. Yuanying pursued the rebels to Yique and besieged them, but for half a month no one dared press the attack.

sentences.zh: 防禦判官王茂元殺一人而後進。

translations.literal: Defense Recorder Wang Maoyuan killed one man and then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Defense Recorder Wang Maoyuan killed one man and only then pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 或有毀其墉而入者，賊眾突出，圍兵奔駭。

translations.literal: Some broke down the wall and entered; the rebel host burst out, and the besieging troops fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: When some broke through the wall and entered, the rebels burst out, and the besieging troops fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 賊乃團結，以其孥偕行。

translations.literal: The rebels then banded together and took their wives and children with them as they went.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then banded together and fled, taking their wives and children with them.

sentences.zh: 出長夏門，轉掠郊墅，奪牛馬，東濟伊水，望山而去。

translations.literal: They went out through Changxia Gate, turned to plunder suburban villas, seized oxen and horses, crossed the Yi River eastward, and fled toward the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They passed out through Changxia Gate, raided suburban estates, seized oxen and horses, crossed the Yi River to the east, and fled toward the mountains.

sentences.zh: 元膺誡境上兵重購以捕之。

translations.literal: Yuanying ordered the border troops to offer heavy rewards for their capture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying ordered the troops along the border to offer large rewards for their capture.

sentences.zh: 數月，有山棚賣鹿於市。

translations.literal: Several months later a mountain shack dweller sold deer in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later a mountain shack dweller came to the market to sell deer.

sentences.zh: 賊過，山棚乃召集其黨，引官兵圍於谷中，盡獲之。

translations.literal: When the rebels passed by, the shack dweller summoned his faction, led government troops to surround them in a valley, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels passed by, the shack dweller summoned his confederates, led government troops to surround the rebels in a valley, and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 窮理其魁，乃中嶽寺僧圓凈，年八十余，嘗為史思明將，偉悍過人。

translations.literal: Investigating to the end, the ringleader was the monk Yuanjing of Zhongyue Temple, over eighty years old, once a general under Shi Siming, magnificent and fierce beyond other men.
translations.idiomatic: When the investigation reached its end, the ringleader proved to be the monk Yuanjing of Zhongyue Temple, more than eighty years old, once a general under Shi Siming, and a man of towering stature and ferocious strength.

sentences.zh: 初執之，使折其脛，錘之不折。

translations.literal: When first seized, they tried to break his shins; hammering them, they would not break.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first seized, they tried to break his shins with hammers, but the bones would not break.

sentences.zh: 圓凈罵曰：「腳猶不解折，乃稱健兒乎！」

translations.literal: Yuanjing cursed, saying: "You cannot even break a leg and yet call yourselves brave warriors!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing cursed them, saying, "You cannot even break a leg and you call yourselves brave warriors!

sentences.zh: 自置其足教折之。

translations.literal: He placed his own foot and taught them how to break it.
translations.idiomatic: He placed his own foot and showed them how to break it.

sentences.zh: 臨刑嘆曰：「誤我事，不得使洛城流血！」

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed and said: "You have ruined my plan—I could not make Luoyang run with blood!"
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he sighed and said, "You have ruined my plan—I was not able to make Luoyang run with blood!

sentences.zh: 死者凡數十人。

translations.literal: Those executed numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen men were executed.

sentences.zh: 留守防禦將二人，都亭驛卒五人，甘水驛卒三人，皆潛受其職署而為之耳目，自始謀及將敗無知者。

translations.literal: Two garrison defense generals, five runners at Duting Station, and three runners at Ganshui Station had all secretly received appointments from them and served as their eyes and ears; from the first plotting until near defeat no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Two garrison defense generals, five runners at Duting Station, and three runners at Ganshui Station had all secretly accepted appointments from the conspirators and served as their informants. From the first plotting until the plot was nearly exposed, no one knew.

sentences.zh: 初，師道多買田於伊闕、陸渾之間，凡十余處，故以舍山棚而衣食之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shidao had bought much land between Yique and Luhun—more than ten places in all—so he lodged mountain shack dwellers there and supported them with food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shidao had purchased extensive lands between Yique and Luhun—more than ten holdings in all—and lodged mountain shack dwellers there to support them with food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 有訾嘉珍、門察者，潛部分之，以屬圓凈。

translations.literal: There were Zi Jiazhen and Men Cha, who secretly divided them up and placed them under Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Two men named Zi Jiazhen and Men Cha secretly organized these men and placed them under Yuanjing's command.

sentences.zh: 以師道錢千萬偽理佛寺，期以嘉珍竊發時舉火於山中，集二縣山棚人作亂。

translations.literal: Using ten million of Shidao's cash they falsely built a Buddhist temple, planning that when Jiazhen launched the secret attack they would raise fire in the mountains and gather the mountain shack people of two counties to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Using ten million cash from Shidao they built a Buddhist temple as a cover, planning that when Jiazhen launched the secret attack they would raise signal fires in the mountains and rally the mountain shack dwellers of two counties in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及窮按之，嘉珍、門察皆稱害武元衡者。

translations.literal: When the investigation was pursued to the end, Jiazhen and Men Cha both declared themselves the killers of Wu Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the investigation was pursued to its end, Jiazhen and Men Cha both claimed to have been the killers of Wu Yuanheng.

sentences.zh: 元膺以聞，送之上都，賞告變人楊進、李再興錦彩三百匹、宅一區，授之郎將。

translations.literal: Yuanying reported this and sent them to the capital; he rewarded the informants Yang Jin and Li Zaixing with three hundred bolts of brocade and one residence, and appointed them as commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying reported the matter and sent the prisoners to the capital. He rewarded the informants Yang Jin and Li Zaixing with three hundred bolts of brocade and a residence, and appointed them commandants.

sentences.zh: 無膺因請募山河子弟以衛宮城，從之。

translations.literal: Yuanying thereupon asked to recruit sons and younger brothers from the hills and rivers to guard the palace city, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying then asked permission to recruit local men from the hills and rivers to guard the palace city, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 盜發之日，都城震恐，留守兵寡弱，不可倚，而元膺坐皇城門，指使部分，氣意自若，以故居人帖然。

translations.literal: On the day the plot broke out the capital was shaken with fear; garrison troops were few and weak and could not be relied on, yet Yuanying sat at the Imperial City gate, directing deployment with calm bearing and untroubled spirit, and so the residents were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the plot broke out the capital was gripped with fear. The garrison troops were few and weak and could not be relied upon, yet Yuanying sat at the gate of the Imperial City, directing the deployment with calm and untroubled bearing, and the residents were reassured.

sentences.zh: 數年，改河中尹，充河中節度等使。

translations.literal: Several years later he was changed to Prefect of Hezhong and appointed Military Governor of Hezhong et al.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was made prefect of Hezhong and appointed military governor of the Hezhong circuit.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮多事姑息，元膺獨以堅正自處，監軍使洎往來中貴，無不敬憚。

translations.literal: At the time regional commands mostly practiced indulgence; Yuanying alone maintained himself with firm uprightness, and army supervisors and eunuch envoys coming and going all feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most regional commanders practiced indulgence, but Yuanying alone maintained himself with firm integrity. Army supervisors and eunuch envoys who passed through his domain all feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 入拜吏部侍郎，因疾固讓，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel; because of illness he firmly declined and was changed to Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, but because of illness he firmly declined the post and was instead made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年二月卒，年七十二，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe he died, aged seventy-two; posthumously granted Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, at the age of seventy-two. He was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元膺學識深遠，處事得體，正色立朝，有臺輔之望。

translations.literal: Yuanying's learning and insight were deep and far-reaching; in handling affairs he was appropriate; he stood at court with stern countenance and had the prospect of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying's learning was deep and his judgment far-reaching. He handled affairs with propriety, stood at court with unwavering integrity, and was regarded as a man destined for the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 初遊京師時，故相齊映謂人曰：「吾不及識婁、郝，殆斯人之類乎！」

translations.literal: When he first traveled in the capital, former chancellor Qi Ying said to others: "I was not able to know Lou and Hao in their time—perhaps this man is of that sort!"
translations.idiomatic: When he first traveled in the capital, the former chancellor Qi Ying said to others, "I never had the chance to know Lou and Hao in their time—perhaps this man is of their kind!

sentences.zh: 其業官行己，始終無缺云。

translations.literal: In his official career and personal conduct from beginning to end he was without fault, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In his official career and personal conduct, from beginning to end he was without reproach.

sentences.zh: 劉棲楚，出於寒微，為吏鎮州，王承宗甚奇之。

translations.literal: Liu Qichu came from humble poverty; he served as an official in Zhenzhou, and Wang Chengzong greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu came from humble origins. He served as an official in Zhen Prefecture, and Wang Chengzong took a great liking to him.

sentences.zh: 後有薦於李逢吉，自鄧掾擢為拾遺。

translations.literal: Later someone recommended him to Li Fengji; from Dengzhou aide he was raised to Remonstrance Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recommended to Li Fengji and was promoted from a staff aide in Deng Prefecture to Remonstrance Clerk.

sentences.zh: 性果敢。

translations.literal: His nature was bold and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resolute by nature.

sentences.zh: 逢吉以為鷹犬之用，欲中傷裴度及殺李紳。

translations.literal: Fengji used him as hawk and hound, wishing to strike at Pei Du and kill Li Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji used him as a political enforcer, intending to ruin Pei Du and have Li Shen killed.

sentences.zh: 無何，遷起居郎，至諫議。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Diarist, then to Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Diarist and then to Remonstrance Adviser.

sentences.zh: 俄又宣授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed by direct edict as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed by direct edict as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 丞郎宣授，未之有也。

translations.literal: Direct edict appointment to a vice-ministerial director post—there had never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: A direct edict appointment to a vice-ministerial director post was unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹，摧抑豪右，甚有鉤距，人多比之於西漢趙廣漢者。

translations.literal: He was changed to Prefect of the Capital District, crushed and suppressed powerful families, and had great skill in investigation; many compared him to Zhao Guanghan of the Western Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of the Capital District, where he crushed the powerful elite with sharp investigative methods. Many compared him to Zhao Guanghan of the Western Han.

sentences.zh: 後恃權寵，常以詞氣淩宰相韋處厚，遂出為桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: Later relying on power and favor he often used overbearing language toward Chancellor Wei Chuhou, and was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, relying on power and imperial favor, he often spoke to Chancellor Wei Chuhou with overbearing arrogance, and was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒於任，時大和元年九月。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died in office, in the ninth month of the first year of Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he died in office, in the ninth month of the first year of Dahe.

sentences.zh: 張宿者，布衣諸生也。

translations.literal: Zhang Su was a commoner scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su was a commoner and a student of the classics.

sentences.zh: 憲宗為廣陵王時，因軍使張茂宗薦達，出入邸第。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was Prince of Guangling, through Army Commissioner Zhang Maozong's recommendation he gained access and came and went in the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong was still Prince of Guangling, he gained access through the recommendation of Army Commissioner Zhang Maozong and came and went freely in the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 及上在東宮，宿時入謁，辯譎敢言。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, Su often entered for audience; he was eloquent, cunning, and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor was in the Eastern Palace, Su often came to audience. He was eloquent, shrewd, and bold in speech.

sentences.zh: 洎監撫之際，驟承顧擢，授左拾遺。

translations.literal: When he came to oversee and nurture affairs, he suddenly received favored promotion and was appointed Left Remonstrance Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince assumed the regency, he was suddenly favored with rapid promotion and appointed Left Remonstrance Clerk.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩數召對禁中，機事不密，貶郴州郴縣丞。

translations.literal: Because of old favor he was repeatedly summoned for audience within the Forbidden Precinct; state secrets were not kept secure, and he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Chen County in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of their old bond he was repeatedly summoned for private audience within the palace, but he failed to keep state secrets secure and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Chen County in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十余年征入，歷贊善大夫、左補闕、比部員外郎。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he was summoned in, passing through Mentor to the Heir Apparent, Left Supplementation Aide, and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later he was recalled to the capital, serving in succession as Mentor to the Heir Apparent, Left Supplementation Aide, and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉惡之，數於上前言其狡譎，不可保信，乃用為濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Fengji hated him and repeatedly said before the throne that he was cunning and deceitful and could not be trusted; he was then appointed Prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Fengji disliked him and repeatedly told the emperor that he was cunning and deceitful and could not be trusted. He was therefore sent out as prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 制下，宿自理乞留，乃追制。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Su himself petitioned with reasons asking to remain, and the edict was then revoked.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict was issued, Su petitioned on his own account to be allowed to stay at court, and the edict was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 上欲以為諫議大夫，逢吉奏曰：「諫議職重，當以能可否朝政者為之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint him Remonstrance Adviser. Fengji memorialized, saying: "The post of Remonstrance Adviser is weighty; it should be filled by one who can approve or disapprove court policy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make him Remonstrance Adviser. Fengji memorialized: "The office of Remonstrance Adviser is a weighty one and should go to someone capable of passing judgment on court policy.

sentences.zh: 宿細人，不足以汙賢者位。

translations.literal: Su is a petty man, not sufficient to defile the seat of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Su is a small-minded man, unworthy to sully a post meant for the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 陛下必須用宿，請先去臣即可。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must use Su, I ask only that you remove me first."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on employing Su, then remove me first—that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又逢吉與裴度是非不同，上方委度討伐，乃出逢吉為劍南東川節度。

translations.literal: Moreover Fengji and Pei Du differed in right and wrong; the emperor was then entrusting Du with punitive campaigns, so Fengji was sent out as Military Governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji and Pei Du also stood on opposite sides of the issues, and as the emperor was then entrusting Du with military campaigns, Fengji was sent out as military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 乃用宿權知諫議大夫，俄而內使宣授。

translations.literal: Su was then appointed acting Remonstrance Adviser; before long an inner palace envoy announced and conferred the post.
translations.idiomatic: Su was then made acting Remonstrance Adviser, and soon an inner palace envoy announced the formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 初，宰相崔群、王涯奏曰：「諫議大夫前時亦有拔自山林、起於卒伍者，其例則少，用皆有由。

translations.literal: Initially chancellors Cui Qun and Wang Ya memorialized, saying: "Remonstrance Adviser in former times was also at times drawn from mountain forests or raised from the ranks; such examples are few, and appointments all had reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, chancellors Cui Qun and Wang Ya had memorialized: "There have indeed been Remonstrance Advisers drawn from reclusion in the mountains or raised from the ranks, but such cases are rare and always had clear justification.

sentences.zh: 或道義彰明，不求聞達；

translations.literal: Some had manifest righteousness and integrity and sought no fame or advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Some had manifest integrity and sought no fame or advancement;

sentences.zh: 或山林卓異，出於群萃。

translations.literal: some were extraordinary among mountain recluses, standing out from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: others were extraordinary recluses who stood out from the multitude.

sentences.zh: 以此選求，是愜公議。

translations.literal: To select and seek by such standards satisfies public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: To choose men by such standards satisfies public opinion.

sentences.zh: 或事跡未著，恩由一時，雖有例超升，即時議未允。

translations.literal: Some whose deeds were not yet established received grace from a moment in time; though there were precedents for extraordinary promotion, contemporary opinion did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Others whose achievements were not yet established received favor in a passing moment; though precedents existed for extraordinary promotion, contemporary opinion did not approve.

sentences.zh: 宿本非文辭入用，望實稍輕。

translations.literal: Su was originally brought into service not through literary skill; his reputation and substance are somewhat slight.
translations.idiomatic: Su was not originally brought into office on the strength of literary talent, and both his reputation and substance are rather slight.

sentences.zh: 驟加不次之榮，翻恐以身為累。

translations.literal: To suddenly add extraordinary honor may instead make a burden of oneself.
translations.idiomatic: To heap extraordinary honor upon him all at once may instead become a burden to him.

sentences.zh: 臣等所以累有論諫，依資且與郎中，事冀適中，非於此人情有厚薄，請授職方郎中。」

translations.literal: We ministers therefore repeatedly remonstrated that, according to seniority, he be given at least a Director post; the matter we hope will be moderate—not that we have partiality regarding this man's worth—we ask that he be appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments."
translations.idiomatic: That is why we have repeatedly remonstrated that, according to seniority, he be given at least a directorship—we hope for a moderate appointment, not because we bear this man any personal favor or disfavor—and we ask that he be made Director in the Bureau of Appointments."

sentences.zh: 上命如初，群等乃請權知，尋又宣援。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered as before; Qun and the others then asked for acting appointment; soon again an envoy announced and conferred it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held to his original order, whereupon Qun and the others asked that Su serve only in an acting capacity—but soon an inner envoy again announced the formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 宿怨執政擯己，頗加讒毀。

translations.literal: Su resented those in power for excluding him and added considerable slander.
translations.idiomatic: Su resented the ruling faction for shutting him out and heaped considerable slander upon them.

sentences.zh: 依附皇甫镈等，傷害清正之士，陰事中要，以圖進取。

translations.literal: He attached himself to Huangfu Bo and others, harmed upright men, secretly worked on important affairs, and sought advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Huangfu Bo and his circle, harmed upright officials, secretly handled weighty matters, and plotted his own advancement.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，充淄青宣慰使，至東都，暴病卒，於是正人相賀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was appointed Pacification Commissioner to Ziqing; upon reaching the Eastern Capital he suddenly fell ill and died, whereupon upright men congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was appointed pacification commissioner to Ziqing. When he reached the Eastern Capital he suddenly fell gravely ill and died, and upright men congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 詔贈秘書監。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 熊望者，登進士第。

translations.literal: Xiong Wang passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wang passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 粗有文詞，而性憸險。

translations.literal: He had rough literary skill, but his nature was crafty and dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: He had some literary skill, but his character was crafty and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 有口辯，往往得遊公卿間，率以大言詭意，指抉時政。

translations.literal: He had eloquence and often gained access among ministers and nobles, generally using grand words and devious intent to point out and expose current policy.
translations.idiomatic: He was glib of tongue and often gained access among high ministers and nobles, generally using grand rhetoric and devious intent to expose and attack current policy.

sentences.zh: 既由此而得進士第，務進不已。

translations.literal: Having thereby obtained jinshi rank, he strove for advancement without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Having obtained his jinshi degree by such means, he strove for advancement without cease.

sentences.zh: 而京兆尹劉棲楚以不次驟居清貫，廣樹朋黨，門庭無晝夜填委不息。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Prefect of Jingzhao Liu Qichu, through extraordinary promotion, suddenly held a pure and exalted post; he widely planted factional ties, and his gate day and night was ceaselessly filled with visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Qichu, prefect of Jingzhao, had through extraordinary promotion suddenly risen to a lofty and honored post. He built up a wide network of factional ties, and his gate was crowded day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 望出入棲楚之門，為伺密機，陰佐計畫，人無知者。

translations.literal: Wang came and went at Qichu's gate, spying on secret affairs and secretly assisting in plans; no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang came and went at Qichu's gate, spying on confidential affairs and secretly helping to devise plans, and no one knew of it.

sentences.zh: 昭湣嬉遊之隙，學為歌詩。

translations.literal: In the intervals of Zhaomin's pleasure-seeking, he learned to compose songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of Emperor Zhaomin's pleasure-seeking, he learned to compose songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士崇重，不可褻狎，乃議別置東頭學士，以備曲宴賦詩，令采卑官才堪任學士者為之。

translations.literal: Because Hanlin Academicians were honored and revered and could not be treated lightly, they proposed separately establishing Eastern Academicians to serve at private banquets for composing poetry, ordering that low-ranking officials whose talent fitted the academician role be selected.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hanlin Academicians were held in high honor and could not be treated casually, the court proposed establishing a separate corps of Eastern Academicians to attend private banquets and compose verse, selecting low-ranking officials whose talent suited the role.

sentences.zh: 棲楚以望名薦送，事未行而昭湣崩。

translations.literal: Qichu recommended Wang by name for submission; before the matter was carried out Zhaomin died.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu recommended Wang by name for the post, but before the plan could be carried out Emperor Zhaomin died.

sentences.zh: 柏耆者，將軍良器之子。

translations.literal: Bai Qi was the son of General Liang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi was the son of General Liang Qi.

sentences.zh: 素負志略，學縱橫家流。

translations.literal: He had long possessed ambition and strategy and studied the persuasion school tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He had long possessed ambition and strategic talent and studied the persuasion school.

sentences.zh: 會王承宗以常山叛，朝廷厭兵，欲以恩澤撫之。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong rebelled at Changshan, the court was weary of warfare and wished to comfort him with imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled at Changshan, the court was weary of war and wished to win him back with imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 耆於蔡州行營以畫幹裴度，請以朝旨奉使鎮州，乃自處士授左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the Caizhou field headquarters Qi used a painted petition to approach Pei Du, asking to be sent on mission to Zhenzhou with imperial decree; he was then appointed Left Remonstrance Clerk from his status as a retired scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At the field headquarters in Caizhou, Qi submitted a painted petition to Pei Du asking to be sent to Zhenzhou on imperial business, and was thereupon appointed Left Remonstrance Clerk from his status as a private scholar.

sentences.zh: 既見承宗，以大義陳說。

translations.literal: After meeting Chengzong, he explained with great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Chengzong, he set forth the case in terms of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 承宗泣下，請質二男，獻兩郡，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chengzong wept, offered his two sons as hostages and surrendered two prefectures; thereby Qi became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong wept, offered his two sons as hostages, and surrendered two commanderies, and thereby Qi became famous.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，王承宗歸國，移鎮滑州，朝廷賜成德軍賞錢一百萬貫，令諫議大夫鄭覃宣慰軍人，賞錢未至，浩浩然騰口。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe year ten Wang Chengzong returned to allegiance and was transferred to govern Huazhou; the court granted the Chengde army reward money of one million strings; Remonstrance Adviser Zheng Tan was ordered to pacify the troops; the reward money had not arrived and voices rose in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, Wang Chengzong returned to allegiance and was transferred to Huazhou. The court granted the Chengde army a reward of one million strings of cash and ordered Remonstrance Adviser Zheng Tan to reassure the troops, but before the money arrived voices of complaint rose in a great clamor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗詔耆往諭旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong ordered Qi to go explain the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong ordered Qi to go and explain the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 耆至，令承宗集三軍，宣導上旨，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: When Qi arrived, he had Chengzong assemble the three armies, proclaimed and guided the emperor's intent, and the troops' hearts were settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi arrived, he had Chengzong assemble the three armies and proclaim the emperor's message, and the troops' minds were calmed.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 太和初，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was promoted to Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was promoted to Remonstrance Adviser.

sentences.zh: 俄而，李同捷叛，兩河籓帥加兵滄、德，宿師於野連年。

translations.literal: Soon Li Tongjie rebelled; governors of the two He circuits added troops at Cang and De; armies encamped in the field year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Tongjie rebelled. Military governors of the two He circuits reinforced their armies at Cang and De, and imperial troops camped in the field year after year.

sentences.zh: 同捷窮蹙求降。

translations.literal: Tongjie, driven to straits, sought to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tongjie, hard pressed, sought to surrender.

sentences.zh: 耆既宣諭訖，與節度使李祐謀。

translations.literal: After Qi finished proclaiming the imperial message, he plotted with Military Governor Li You.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi had finished proclaiming the imperial message, he plotted with Military Governor Li You.

sentences.zh: 耆乃帥數百騎入滄州，取同捷赴京。

translations.literal: Qi then led several hundred horsemen into Cangzhou, took Tongjie and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qi then led several hundred horsemen into Cangzhou, seized Tongjie, and escorted him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 滄、德平。

translations.literal: Cang and De were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cang and De were pacified.

sentences.zh: 諸將害耆邀功，爭上表論列。

translations.literal: The generals resented Qi for seizing merit and vied to submit memorials arguing the case.
translations.idiomatic: The generals resented Qi for stealing their credit and vied to submit memorials arguing against him.

sentences.zh: 文宗不獲已，貶循州司戶判官，沈亞之貶虔州南康尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong had no choice; Qi was demoted to Secretary of the Revenue Bureau in Xunzhou as acting, and Shen Yazhi was demoted to Marshal of Nankang in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong, having no choice, demoted Qi to acting secretary of the revenue bureau in Xun Prefecture, and Shen Yazhi to marshal of Nankang in Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 內官馬國亮又奏耆於同捷處取婢九人，再命長流愛州，尋賜死。

translations.literal: Eunuch Ma Guoliang further reported that Qi had taken nine maidservants from Tongjie's household; he was again ordered exiled far to Aizhou, and soon was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ma Guoliang further reported that Qi had taken nine maidservants from Tongjie's household. Qi was again ordered into distant exile at Aizhou, and soon was granted death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：人臣事君，犯顏匡政，不避死亡之誅。

translations.literal: The historian says: When ministers serve their lord, to confront him face to face and correct policy, not avoiding the punishment of death—
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When a minister serves his ruler, to speak bluntly to his face and set policy aright, not shrinking from the penalty of death—

sentences.zh: 議者以為徇名，臣惡其訐也。

translations.literal: Critics thought it was for fame; this minister detests such censoriousness.
translations.idiomatic: Critics may call it courting fame, but this historian detests such faultfinding.

sentences.zh: 如許京兆之劾軍吏，呂尚書之封詔書，詞義可觀，聳動人聽，以為沽激，傷善何多！

translations.literal: Such as Prefect of Jingzhao Xu's impeachment of army officials and Minister Lu's sealing of the edict—word and meaning were admirable and stirring to listeners—yet to be judged as fishing for acclaim: how much good was harmed!
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Xu, prefect of Jingzhao, who impeached army officials, and Lu, the minister, who sealed back an edict—their words were admirable and stirred all who heard them—yet to dismiss them as fishing for acclaim: how much good was lost!

sentences.zh: 而棲楚、張宿之徒，鷹犬下材，為人鳴吠，誠可醜也。

translations.literal: Whereas Qichu, Zhang Su and their kind were base talent fit only as hawk and hound, barking for others—truly repulsive.
translations.idiomatic: By contrast, Qichu, Zhang Su, and their like were base talent fit only to serve as hawk and hound, barking on others' behalf—truly contemptible.

sentences.zh: 柏耆恃縱橫之算，欲俯拾卿相，忘身蹈利，旋踵而誅，宜哉！

translations.literal: Bai Qi relied on persuader's schemes, wished to stoop and pick up ministerial posts, forgot himself in pursuit of profit, and within a turning of the heel was executed—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi relied on the arts of the persuaders, hoped to stoop and pluck up ministerial rank, forgot himself in the rush for profit, and was executed within a turning of the heel—fitting indeed!

sentences.zh: 巢父使不辱命，誌在致君，遭罹喪亂，竟陷虎吻。

translations.literal: Chaofu as envoy did not disgrace his charge; his aim was to bring the lord to perfection; he met with calamity and chaos and in the end fell into the tiger's maw.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu as envoy did not disgrace his mission; his aim was to bring his ruler to perfection. He met calamity and chaos and in the end fell into the tiger's maw.

sentences.zh: 而戣、戢諸子，世載忠貞，大中之後，郁為昌族。

translations.literal: Yet the sons Ke and Ji generation upon generation bore loyal integrity; after the Dazhong reign they flourished as a noble clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ke, Ji, and the other sons generation upon generation bore loyal integrity, and after the Dazhong reign they flourished into a noble clan.

sentences.zh: 為善之利，豈虛言哉！

translations.literal: The profit of doing good—is it empty talk!
translations.idiomatic: The reward of doing good—is that empty talk!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君子重義，小人殉利。

translations.literal: In praise: The noble person esteems righteousness; the petty person dies for profit.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The noble person esteems righteousness; the petty person dies for profit.

sentences.zh: 巢殞耆誅，其道即異。

translations.literal: Chaofu perished and Qi was executed—their Way was immediately different.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu perished and Qi was executed—their paths were utterly unlike.

sentences.zh: 許、呂封駁，照耀黃扉。

translations.literal: Xu and Lu's sealed remonstrances illuminated the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Lu's sealed remonstrances shone upon the yellow gate of the palace.

sentences.zh: 死而可作，吾誰與歸？

translations.literal: If among the dead one could still act, with whom would I go?
translations.idiomatic: If the dead could yet act, with whom would I align myself?
